subject: nursery web spider
title: This Spider Gift-Wraps Garbage for His Date, Then Plays Dead to Survive It

scenes.text: This male spider brings his date a present. A third of the time, it's garbage.
Nursery web spider males wrap a dead insect in silk and hand it over before mating. She eats while he gets on with it.
But in the wild, about 38 percent of the parcels hold an empty husk or a seed. Nicely wrapped, worthless inside.
It works. In the lab, one in six males with no gift mated. Twelve of thirteen with a fake gift did.
The females aren't fooled for long. Once they taste the fake, they cut the mating short.
And if she grabs the gift and might grab him, he goes limp and plays dead, still clinging to the parcel.

description:
Male nursery web spiders hand females a silk-wrapped gift before mating, and many of the gifts are fakes.
In Pisaura mirabilis, about 62 percent of gifts collected in the wild held fresh prey; the rest held empty insect husks or plant parts wrapped in silk. In experiments by Maria Albo, Trine Bilde and colleagues at Aarhus University (BMC Evolutionary Biology, 2011), males with no gift rarely mated (1 of 6), while 12 of 13 males offering a worthless gift mated, about as often as males with a real fly. Females shorten the mating once they discover the gift is worthless, and fewer eggs hatch when no gift is given. Males also play dead while the female holds the gift, keeping a grip on it, a behaviour seen mostly with edible gifts.
Would you accept a beautifully wrapped empty box?
first_comment: Twelve of thirteen males got away with a fake gift. Is there a worse dating trick anywhere in nature?
